input.strategy_title: Bring-your-own vector database for RAG workloads
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

RAG applications built on Llama Stack need a vector store, and today the
platform neither ships one nor documents how to attach an external one.
Customers are split into two camps with incompatible expectations: regulated
customers want a platform-managed vector database with supported images and
lifecycle, while cloud-native customers already run managed services (e.g.
a cloud vector DB) and only want a sanctioned way to connect them. We have not
decided which posture to productize first, and the answer changes most of the
downstream work.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A decision is reached, with a documented evaluation, on the first supported vector store posture: platform-managed (operator-deployed Milvus) versus external-connection-only. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Depending on that decision: either administrators can deploy the managed vector store through the Platform Operator with productized images, or data scientists can register an external vector store connection per project with validated connectivity. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Llama Stack distributions can consume the chosen vector store as a RAG provider without hand-editing distribution configs. |
| HLR-4 | P1 | The Dashboard exposes the chosen integration (deploy-and-manage UI for the managed path, or connection management UI for the external path). |
| HLR-5 | P2 | Product documentation covers setup and limits for whichever posture ships. |

## Affected Components

- Llama Stack
- Dashboard
- Platform Operator

## Out of Scope

- Shipping both postures in the same release
- Embedding model selection and lifecycle (separate strategy)

## Open Questions

1. Managed Milvus versus external-connection-only is genuinely undecided — the
   evaluation in HLR-1 must weigh supportability cost, disconnected-environment
   viability, and time-to-market, and the outcome forks the implementation
   structure for HLR-2 through HLR-5.

# Midstream repo onboarding for the managed vector store (Milvus)

## Description

Creates the midstream home for the vector database that the platform-managed
posture will ship: a fork/import of upstream Milvus under the opendatahub-io
GitHub organization, positioned for productized images and lifecycle
management by the platform. This epic exists only if the posture decision
selects the platform-managed path.

## Scope

- Create the midstream Milvus repository under opendatahub-io following the
  established midstream fork process (branching/model matching the other
  opendatahub-io midstream repos).
- Import the chosen upstream Milvus version and record the upstream tracking
  policy (how updates flow).
- Apply the minimum productization adjustments needed for the repo to build a
  container image in the midstream (no feature work — deployment logic and
  platform integration live elsewhere).
- Document repo ownership and component mapping (a canonical Jira component
  for the vector store should be requested, since none exists today).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The midstream repository exists under opendatahub-io with the agreed name
  and branch model, populated from the selected upstream Milvus version.
- The repo builds a container image from its default branch using standard
  midstream tooling.
- The upstream tracking/versioning policy is documented in the repo.
- Ownership and on-call/maintenance responsibility are recorded, and a Jira
  component request for the vector store is filed.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)**, managed-path clause: "administrators can deploy the managed
  vector store through the Platform Operator with productized images" — this
  epic is the prerequisite that makes productized images possible.

# License validation for Milvus and its transitive dependencies

## Description

Runs license scanning and validation over the midstream vector store (Milvus)
and its transitive dependencies to confirm the platform-managed posture can
ship productized images without license blockers. This epic exists only if
the posture decision selects the platform-managed path.

## Scope

- Run the standard license scanning tooling over the Milvus source and its
  transitive dependency tree.
- Triage findings: identify copyleft or otherwise problematic licenses that
  would affect shipping productized images.
- Record the license verdict and any required remediations (dependency
  exclusions, alternative versions) as an input to the operator-side
  deployment implementation.
- Escalate unresolved legal questions through the license review process.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A complete license scan report exists for Milvus and its transitive
  dependencies.
- Every finding is triaged with a documented disposition (acceptable,
  remediated, or escalated).
- No unresolved license blocker remains for shipping productized Milvus
  images, or the blocker and its fallback are documented and handed to the
  deployment implementation.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)**, managed-path clause: productized images require a clean
  license position; this epic gates the managed deployment work.

# Konflux onboarding for the midstream vector store repo

## Description

Onboards the midstream vector store (Milvus) repository to Konflux so its
container images are built, scanned, and released through the standard
platform build pipeline. This epic exists only if the posture decision
selects the platform-managed path.

## Scope

- Create the Konflux application and components for the midstream vector
  store repo using the known onboarding recipe.
- Wire the build pipeline to the repo's default branch with the standard
  build/test tasks.
- Verify the pipeline produces a signed, scannable image in the expected
  registry namespace.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Konflux application exists for the midstream vector store repo and is
  linked to the correct Git repository and branch.
- A full pipeline run completes green on the default branch, producing an
  image in the expected registry.
- Release/integration targets are configured per the standard recipe.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)**, managed-path clause: "productized images" — the build
  pipeline is what productizes the image consumed by the managed deployment.

# Platform Operator support for deploying the managed vector store

## Description

Extends the Platform Operator so administrators can deploy the managed vector
store (Milvus) into their cluster with productized images and platform
lifecycle (install, upgrade, health, removal). This is the core managed-path
delivery for HLR-2 and exists only if the posture decision selects the
platform-managed path.

## Scope

- Implement operator-side deployment and lifecycle management for the managed
  vector store, at the capability level described by the strategy (the
  concrete CRD shape, reconciliation approach, and sizing defaults are design
  decisions for the implementing team).
- Reference the productized Milvus image produced by the midstream build
  pipeline (pinned digest at release time — a configuration reference, not a
  build-time coupling).
- Surface deployment status and health in the standard operator status
  conditions so cluster administrators and the Dashboard can observe it.
- Include disconnected-environment support consistent with the posture
  evaluation outcome (no reliance on external image pulls at deploy time).

## Acceptance Criteria

- An administrator can deploy the managed vector store through the Platform
  Operator on a vanilla cluster, and it reaches a healthy running state.
- The deployment uses the productized image with a pinned digest available
  from the build pipeline (acceptance gate on the parallel build-pipeline
  work; not a DAG dependency).
- The build pipeline for any changed operator code is green (standard
  pipeline acceptance for operator changes).
- Upgrade and removal of the managed vector store work without manual cleanup
  steps.
- Deployment succeeds in a disconnected environment using mirrored images.
- The operator deployment model chosen during implementation is validated
  against the (currently missing) architecture context for the Platform
  Operator, and any divergence is fed back to the architecture record.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)**, managed-path clause: "administrators can deploy the managed
  vector store through the Platform Operator with productized images."

# Llama Stack RAG provider integration for the managed vector store

## Description

Makes Llama Stack distributions consume the platform-managed vector store as
a RAG provider without hand-editing distribution configs: when a distribution
runs alongside the operator-deployed Milvus, the vector provider is wired in
through the platform's configuration surface rather than manual edits. This
epic exists only if the posture decision selects the platform-managed path.

## Scope

- Wire the managed vector store into Llama Stack's provider-plugin model as
  the RAG/vector provider, using the deployment interface exposed by the
  Platform Operator (the exact CR fields and config mapping are design
  decisions for the implementing team).
- Ensure distributions pick up the vector provider automatically when the
  managed store is deployed in scope, with no hand-edited distribution
  configs.
- Verify RAG workflows (embedding storage and retrieval) work end-to-end
  against the managed store.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Llama Stack distribution deployed where the managed vector store is
  available uses it as the RAG/vector provider with no manual config edits.
- Document-level ingestion and retrieval through the RAG API succeed against
  the managed store.
- The integration follows the existing provider-plugin pattern in the
  Llama Stack distribution (validated against the Llama Stack architecture
  context).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P1)**: "Llama Stack distributions can consume the chosen vector
  store as a RAG provider without hand-editing distribution configs" —
  managed-posture fulfillment.

# Dashboard deploy-and-manage UI for the managed vector store

## Description

Exposes the platform-managed vector store in the Dashboard: administrators
can deploy it, observe its status, and manage its lifecycle from the console,
following the Dashboard's existing per-component integration pattern (reads
and writes the operator's CRs; owns no data plane). This epic exists only if
the posture decision selects the platform-managed path.

## Scope

- Add a Dashboard surface for deploying the managed vector store
  (creation flow, status views, and lifecycle actions), built against the CRD
  the Platform Operator exposes.
- Gate the surface behind the standard per-component feature flag mechanism
  (OdhDashboardConfig) so it can be enabled per deployment.
- Keep the implementation consistent with the Dashboard architecture
  context: Kubernetes API only, no private component APIs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An administrator can deploy the managed vector store from the Dashboard
  and see its status and health.
- Lifecycle actions offered in the UI map 1:1 to operator capabilities; no
  UI-only state is introduced.
- The integration is behind a feature flag, default off until the managed
  posture ships.
- The UI handles the operator's status conditions faithfully, including
  in-progress and error states.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P1)**: "The Dashboard exposes the chosen integration
  (deploy-and-manage UI for the managed path)."

# External vector store connection registration with validated connectivity

## Description

Implements the sanctioned way for data scientists to register an external
vector store connection per project with validated connectivity: a
platform-managed connection resource that records the external store's
endpoint and credentials, validates reachability, and is consumable by
platform components. This is the core external-path delivery for HLR-2 and
exists only if the posture decision selects the external-connection-only
path.

## Scope

- Implement per-project external vector store connection registration
  (resource shape, credential handling, and namespace/project scoping are
  design decisions for the implementing team).
- Implement connectivity validation at registration time: endpoint
  reachability and credential correctness are checked before the connection
  is accepted, with a clear validation result surfaced to the user.
- Store and expose connection metadata in a form that Llama Stack
  distributions and the Dashboard can consume.
- Keep credential handling consistent with the platform's existing
  secret/credential patterns.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A data scientist can register an external vector store connection in a
  project, supplying endpoint and credentials.
- Registration validates connectivity end-to-end; a connection that fails
  validation is rejected or flagged with a precise error.
- Connections are scoped per project and not visible across projects.
- Registered connections are discoverable by platform components (Llama
  Stack distributions, Dashboard) without manual config.
- Credential material is stored per the platform's secret-handling rules and
  never surfaced in plain text.

  external vector store connection per project with validated connectivity."

# Decide the first supported vector store posture (platform-managed vs external-connection-only)

## Description

This investigation resolves the strategy's gating open question: which vector
store posture the platform productizes first — a platform-managed vector
database (operator-deployed Milvus with productized images and lifecycle) or
an external-connection-only posture (data scientists register an existing
external vector store, e.g. a cloud-managed service, per project). The
deliverable is a documented evaluation and a decision record that selects one
posture and determines the downstream implementation structure.

## Scope

- Evaluate both postures against the criteria named in the strategy:
  supportability cost, disconnected-environment viability, and
  time-to-market.
- Assess what each posture implies for the platform: image productization and
  lifecycle management burden for the managed path; connectivity validation,
  security, and per-project registration semantics for the external path.
- Produce a decision record (ADR-style) recommending the first supported
  posture, with the evaluation documented and trade-offs made explicit.
- Confirm the concrete downstream scope implied by the chosen posture (which
  components change and what each must deliver).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A written evaluation exists covering supportability cost,
  disconnected-environment viability, and time-to-market for both postures.
- A decision is recorded selecting exactly one posture as the first supported
  vector store integration, with rationale traceable to the evaluation.
- The decision record enumerates the downstream work the chosen posture
  implies (component-level scope), so implementation epics can be confirmed
  or re-scoped.
- Stakeholders (product and the affected component teams) have signed off on
  the decision.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: A decision is reached, with a documented evaluation, on the
  first supported vector store posture. This epic is the entire fulfillment
  of HLR-1 and gates all HLR-2 through HLR-5 work.
